structured_output.title: Gamepad controls
structured_output.summary: Add standard-mapping gamepad support through the Gamepad API (`navigator.getGamepads()`), polled each time the game reads input for a sim step and merged into the same `CarInput` as keyboard and touch. Left stick X steers analogue across −1…+1, rescaled past a 0.15 dead-zone so a resting stick gives exactly 0. D-pad left/right steer −1/+1, right trigger (button 7) is gas and left trigger (button 6) brake/reverse. Steer is clamped to −1…+1 when combined with keys or touch. On menus, a fresh press of A (button 0) activates the focused button of the visible menu screen: RACE on the start screen, NEXT RACE on the results screen. Holding A never repeats, and A does nothing to the car mid-race. The pause screen is out of scope tonight because the game loop is stopped while paused.

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `navigator.getGamepads()` mocked to return one connected pad with mapping 'standard', the combined input's read() gives the same CarInput as the equivalent key: d-pad left (button 14) = ArrowLeft {steer:-1,throttle:false,brake:false}, d-pad right (15) = ArrowRight, right trigger (7) = ArrowUp, left trigger (6) = ArrowDown.

Left stick X (axes[0]) steers analogue: −1 reads steer −1 and +1 reads steer +1, exactly as ArrowLeft/ArrowRight do. 0.6 gives a steer strictly between 0 and 1 and larger than 0.4 does. −0.6 gives the negation of 0.6.

Stick dead-zone: when |axes[0]| ≤ 0.15 (e.g. 0.12, −0.1, 0.15), read() gives steer exactly 0 with no buttons pressed, so a resting stick never drifts. Just past it (0.2), steer is above 0 and below 0.1.

Triggers are boolean: a trigger reading value 1 (pressed true) counts as held, and one reading value 0.1 (pressed false) does not. Gamepad steer combined with a held arrow key stays within −1…+1. Pads whose mapping isn't 'standard', null slots and a missing `navigator.getGamepads` are ignored, and keyboard input still works.
On the start screen, with a mocked pad, pressing A (button 0) and running an animation frame starts a race: state().mode becomes 'race' with six cars, the same as tapping RACE.

A acts only on a fresh press. If A is still held from the start screen when the race begins, nothing more is triggered. Once the player has finished and the results screen shows, A held across frames does nothing until it is released and pressed again, which then activates NEXT RACE (a new race on the next track).
During a race with no menu screen showing, pressing A changes nothing: the player's CarInput keeps steer 0 with throttle and brake false, and the game stays in the race, not paused.

playtest.whatYoullSee: A game controller now drives the car. The left stick steers smoothly, so small pushes give gentle turns, and the d-pad steers fully left or right. The right trigger is gas and the left trigger brakes and reverses. The A button presses RACE on the start screen and NEXT RACE on the results screen.
howToTest: Pair a Bluetooth game controller (Xbox or PlayStation style) with your phone, or plug one into a computer, then open the preview.
Press any button on the controller so the browser notices it, then press A on the start screen. A race should start.
Leave the stick alone during the countdown and the race. The car should not creep left or right on its own.
Hold the right trigger to drive and steer with the left stick: small pushes should turn gently and full pushes sharply. Try the d-pad too, and use the left trigger to brake and reverse.
Finish the race. On the results screen, press A: it should start the next race. Holding A down should not keep skipping screens.
